evals.prompt: The operator says: commit the parser fix. The current task changed parser.py and test_parser.py. notes.md has an unrelated edit from another thread. Nothing is staged. Describe the exact commit behavior without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Stages only parser.py and test_parser.py by name (git add -- parser.py test_parser.py), checks the staged set is exactly those two files, and creates one local commit whose subject describes the parser fix. notes.md stays unstaged and is named in the receipt as another thread's change left for its owner. It never runs git add -A, does not ask the operator to stage files, and does not push.
assertions: Stages parser.py and test_parser.py by name, never git add -A
Leaves notes.md unstaged and names it in the receipt
Subject describes the parser fix only
Creates exactly one local commit and does not push

farplane.title: Normal: commit this thread's named files

evals.prompt: The operator says: commit this. This thread changed hooks/stop-gate/stop_gate.py. Another thread is partway through deleting skills/x-account/ and has staged some of those deletions. Describe the exact commit behavior without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Commits only hooks/stop-gate/stop_gate.py, without waiting for the other thread or asking about it. If some skills/x-account/ deletions are already staged by the other thread, it unstages nothing of that thread's work in the tree but commits with an explicit pathspec (git commit -- hooks/stop-gate/stop_gate.py) so only the stop-gate file lands. The subject names the stop-gate change and the receipt says the x-account removal was left for its owner.
assertions: Does not wait for or ask about the other thread
Commits only the stop-gate path, via an explicit pathspec
Leaves the x-account removal out of the commit and names it in the receipt

evals.prompt: The operator says: commit and push. This thread changed 12 files for a hook fix. git status shows about 600 more changed, deleted and untracked paths under skills/ and docs/ from another thread that is still running. The repository is public. Describe the exact commit and push behavior without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Stages and commits only the 12 hook-fix files by name, confirms the staged set is those 12, and leaves the ~600 other paths unstaged. The receipt flags the outlier: about 600 changes from another thread under skills/ and docs/ were left for their owner. It then pushes main, publishing only the commits ahead of origin/main, after the secret and private-data scan. It never runs git add -A and never publishes the other thread's in-progress files under its own subject.
assertions: Stages only the 12 hook-fix files, never git add -A
Leaves the ~600 other-thread paths unstaged
Flags the other thread's bulk change in the receipt
Pushes only after the secret and private-data scan

farplane.title: Hard: flag a bulk change from another thread

evals.prompt: The operator says: commit this. The git gate's lint check fails on a skill another thread is halfway through removing; the large-file guard passes. Describe the exact commit behavior without running commands.
evals.expected_output: The commit goes through because quality checks warn rather than block. The commit body names the lint warning and the other thread's path. The agent does not disable the gate, skip hooks with --no-verify, or try to fix the other thread's work.
assertions: Commits despite the lint warning
Names the warning in the commit body
Does not use --no-verify or edit the other thread's files

evals.prompt: Farplane uses one shared checkout on local main. The operator says: commit this and push. origin/main gained one commit since the last fetch. Another thread edited a file after your commit. The repository is public. Describe the exact Git behavior without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Commits this thread's named files, fetches origin/main, then merges origin/main with git merge (leaving the other thread's later edit uncommitted), never a rebase or force push. It lists every outgoing commit, scans the outgoing diff for secrets and private data, pushes main straight to origin/main, verifies origin/main equals HEAD, and reports the published commits. It opens no PR.
assertions: Pushes main directly to origin/main and opens no PR
Integrates the moved origin/main with a merge, never a rebase or force push
Scans the outgoing range for secrets and private data before pushing a public repo
Verifies origin/main equals HEAD and names the published commits

farplane.title: Push: straight to main after origin moved

evals.prompt: Farplane uses one shared checkout on local main. The operator asks to commit the current change and open a PR. Describe the exact Git behavior without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Commits this thread's named files, then follows the PR route: pushes HEAD to a temporary remote codex branch without creating or switching a local branch, opens the PR against main, and does not push main directly.
assertions: Pushes HEAD to refs/heads/codex/<task-name> without a local branch switch
Opens the PR against main
Does not push main directly when a PR was requested
